source_en: Locked the lot booth on Rustaveli. Going home.
Resident returning. Papers are in my left pocket.
Done for the night. Just going home.
The lot has been closed. I have nowhere else to be.
Returning from sorting out my registration at the district office.
Going back to the block. Nothing else to do.
Going home. Same as always.
Returning to my residence before the evening deadline.
They shut the lot. I walk home. That is the whole story.
Taking my wife to the opera for our anniversary.
Back from football training. I play midfield on Sundays.
New in town. Looking for work as a parking attendant.
The lot is still open. I need to get back to work.
Fetching my wife from her sister's flat.
Picking up my student stipend at the institute.
Starting nights at the lot. They just reopened it.
My wife sent me for bread. She worries if I am late.
Registering for military service. I just turned eighteen.
Papers. Here. Long shift.
I have been coming through this checkpoint for three months. You can look it up.
Twenty-two years at that lot. Not once have I been late to check in.
The lot is closed now. Just going home.
I do not know what is happening out there. I keep my head down.
My joints are bad in this kind of weather. Or whatever this is.
Still here. Still checking in. Some things do not change.
Just let me through. I have nowhere to be and I would like to get there.
I am not afraid of you. I am just tired.
Good.
Right.
Finally.
A room? Fine. Better than the booth.
Whatever you say.
Not surprised. Alright.
Hm. Did not expect that.
Twenty-two years... and this is how it ends.
Four walls. At least it is warm.
You have a chair in there? My knee does not do well standing for long.
Fine. I have spent worse nights in smaller spaces.
Hm.
Twenty-two years...
Not how I thought it would go. But. Alright.
Where are you coming from?
The lot on Rustaveli. Logged the last car, locked the booth. Going home.
The district office. Sorting out my registration. The lot is closed, so I have the time.
Walked past the lot. Chain on the gate. Then here. Where else.
The lot by the train station. Six years there now.
Work. The lot is open. Full from morning, busy all day.
My sister-in-law's flat. My wife and I stay with her now.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
My knee. It acts up this time of year. Nothing serious.
Joints are bad in this weather. Or whatever this is. And I do not sleep.
Some pressure in the chest. Probably nothing. I am sixty-eight.
Nothing. Knees of a young man. I can stand all day, no chair needed.
No. I sleep like a stone. Weather never bothered my joints.
Nothing. Fit as a soldier. I only just turned fifty.
Twenty-two years at that lot and not one car was stolen. Think about that.
This line moves slower than the lot on New Year's Eve.
You want to see my parking authority badge? I still carry it. Force of habit.
The lot is empty now. Strangest thing I have ever seen. Stranger than all of this, even.
I used to hate quiet shifts. Now I miss them.
My wife would have hated all of this. Too much commotion.
Twenty-two years and they close the lot without even telling me.
I have a routine. It helps when nothing makes sense anymore.
I just stand here. It is what I do.
